v2/common/aspose-cli-command.description: Aspose CLI: read, edit, convert and render documents with the Aspose engines. Every command prints JSON; 'schema' lists the commands and the documents that describe them.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --license
options.description: Path to an Aspose license file; overrides every other license source.

options.name: --license-mode
options.description: evaluation reads no license source and runs this command in evaluation mode; by default the license sources are resolved in order. Cannot be combined with --license.

options.name: --max-input-bytes
options.description: Maximum bytes admitted for one input before product runtime initialization. Default: 1073741824. Range: 1-4294967296.

options.name: --output-format
options.description: How results print: the contract envelope, indented or on one line. Default: json.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Emit structured JSONL diagnostics (timing, error codes) to stderr; stdout is untouched.

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --workdir
options.description: Base directory for relative paths. Default: the current directory.

v2/common/budget-list.description: The budgets document of aspose-cli schema: the resource budgets and their limits.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

resourceBudgets.description: The budgets every command applies, in ordinal order of their kinds.

products.description: Each product's own budgets, in product order.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

productBudgets.description: The budgets one product applies to what it loads.

v2/common/command.description: A <command>-command document of aspose-cli schema: one command's options and arguments, as the command line parses them.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

path.description: Full command path, e.g. aspose-cli cells read.

options.description: Options the command accepts, in ordinal order of their names.

arguments.description: Positional arguments the command accepts, in order.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

commandArgument.description: One positional argument accepted by a command.

type.description: The argument's value type, e.g. string.

inputKind.description: What the value names: a file or a JSON source; omitted when it names nothing to read.

valueSource.description: Where the value comes from: the command line, the environment variable it names, or standard input.

secret.description: Whether the value is a secret that is never echoed.

required.description: Whether the command needs the argument.

hasDefault.description: Whether the argument has a default value.

default.description: The default value as text, when there is one.

allowedValues.description: The only values the argument accepts; empty when it accepts any.

commandOption.description: One option accepted by a command.

aliases.description: Other names the option answers to.

type.description: The option's value type, e.g. string or boolean.

required.description: Whether the command needs the option.

recursive.description: Whether the option applies to the command's subcommands too.

hasDefault.description: Whether the option has a default value.

default.description: The default value as text, when there is one.

allowedValues.description: The only values the option accepts; empty when it accepts any.

secret.description: Whether the value is a secret that is never echoed.

valueSource.description: Where the value comes from: the command line, the environment variable it names, or standard input.

inputKind.description: What the value names: a file or a JSON source; omitted when it names nothing to read.

v2/common/diagnostic-details.description: Base schema for product-owned diagnostic details: an object whose members a product may narrow without changing the common envelope.

v2/common/diagnostic-list.description: The diagnostics document of aspose-cli schema: every error and warning code.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

owner.description: What declares the code: common (the SDK), host or a product id.

severity.description: Whether the code names an error or a warning.

exitCode.description: Process exit code of an error; omitted for a warning.

category.description: What kind of problem the code reports, such as validation.

detailsSchemaId.description: Id of the schema of the code's details object.

v2/common/dry-run-result.description: Result of --dry-run on a command that writes files, other than an edit, which applies its operations in memory and reports them in its own result: the command line and the files it names were checked, and nothing ran or was written. A dry run that succeeds does not guarantee that the command succeeds.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

dryRun.description: Always true: the command ran nothing and wrote no file.

checked.description: What the dry run checked, in a fixed order.

paths.description: The absolute paths the command would write, replace or delete: an output file, beside which a command that writes several parts numbers them, or a directory it writes into. Omitted when the command would write nothing, such as a compare without an output.

format.description: The format id the command would write its output file in; omitted for a directory.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

v2/common/engine-warning.description: A warning the document engine reported through its warning callback, as it reported it.

during.description: When the engine reported it: load (opening the input), save (writing the output) or reopen (opening the saved output again).

type.description: The engine's warning type, by its member name.

description.description: The engine's description, as it is.

v2/common/error.description: The single error shape of the CLI, written to stderr when a command fails. Exit codes are coarse and frozen; code carries the precise, machine-readable meaning.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this error conforms to.

v2/common/error-payload.description: Error details: the message states the fact and details carries structured context, often including the valid alternatives.

code.description: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE error code, e.g. ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

details.description: Structured context, e.g. {"requested": "Salez", "available": ["Sales"]}. Its keys come from one dictionary, each described here; no value is null.

actual.description: The measured amount of a budget, in unit.

actualExists.description: Whether the output existed when publication found it changed.

actualSha256.description: The SHA-256 the file had when the command found it changed.

actualSizeBytes.description: The size the file had when the command found it changed.

argument.description: The positional argument the error is about, such as file.

at.description: The object table address the error is about, such as slide/256/shape/3.

available.description: The names or values that exist or are accepted, at most 50.

availableCount.description: How many names or values exist or are accepted.

bookmarks.description: The outline addresses of the bookmarks a warning is about, such as 1/2.

cause.description: Why an operation field was refused.

content.description: The kinds of content an output leaves out, each one of these tokens.

oneOf.description: Files embedded in the document, such as the attachments of a PDF.
The bookmarks of the document's outline.
Charts as charts with their data: the output holds only a picture of them, or none.
Comments as comments: the output writes their text into the body, draws them in balloons beside its pages, or leaves them out.
Editing restrictions, such as a read-only protection of the document.
Form fields: inputs the output has no field for.
The presentation of a PDF portfolio, such as its file list layout; its files stay plain attachments.
Tracked changes as revisions a reader can accept or reject.
Sections, such as the sections of a deck.
Drawings other than charts and pictures, such as shapes, text boxes and groups.
Table styles: the fills, borders and text formatting a table's style gives it.

declared.description: The product the command or extension declares.

detected.description: The products whose formats the content matches.

diagnosticId.description: The host diagnostic id of a startup or process failure.

directory.description: The directory the error is about.

dpi.description: The resolution of a render, in dots per inch.

engineException.description: The type of the exception the document engine threw, such as System.ArgumentException.

errors.description: Every problem, when there are several.

expectedExists.description: Whether the output existed when the command read it.

expectedSha256.description: The SHA-256 the file had when the command read it.

expectedSizeBytes.description: The size the file had when the command read it.

extension.description: The file extension the error is about.

feature.description: The feature the product or format does not support.

field.description: The operation field the error is about.

fields.description: The full names of the form fields the error is about.

format.description: The format id the error is about.

height.description: The height of a render, in pixels.

id.description: The id of the failing operation, as its applied[] entry states it.

index.description: The position of the failing operation in an object table batch's ops, from 0.

list.description: The result field holding a list that was capped, such as outline.

notSupplied.description: The resources a document names that the CLI's resource loader supplied no bytes for, each as {reference, reason}: the reference as the document writes it and why nothing was supplied, such as a network address.

offset.description: The byte offset of the problem in an input.

op.description: The op name of the failing operation.

operation.description: The product feature the error is about.

option.description: The option the error is about, such as --pages.

originalError.description: The error that stopped a publication: its code and details.

originalPath.description: Where the original that a publication moved aside is now, when the publication could not move it back.

path.description: The absolute path of the file the error is about.

phase.description: The stage of processing that failed.

product.description: The product the error is about.

profile.description: The conformance profile the error is about.

range.description: The range or selection as the caller wrote it.

reason.description: Why the value or file was refused, as a short kebab-case token such as unknown-field; the message explains it.

recoveryComplete.description: Whether every publication target was restored.

requested.description: The name, number, value or path as the caller wrote it.

row.description: The object table row the error is about, such as fill.color.

sheet.description: The worksheet the error is about.

source.description: The source of a value, such as a variable or file.

subject.description: What was looked up, such as sheet, page or file.

target.description: The target the error is about.

targets.description: The publication targets and their state; a target whose original was not moved back names where it is (originalPath).

timeoutSeconds.description: The timeout that elapsed, in seconds.

unit.description: The unit of a budget's limit and actual.

variable.description: The environment variable the error is about.

width.description: The width of a render, in pixels.

v2/common/font-list.description: Result of aspose-cli fonts list: the font environment of each product engine — the default fallback font and the sources it scans. Answers "where does this build look for fonts, and what does it fall back to" so a "renders wrong on the server" problem can be traced to font configuration.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

products.description: One entry per product, in catalog order: every product with font diagnostics, or only the one --product names.

license.description: License mode the engine ran under; omitted when it ran licensed.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

fontSource.description: One place the engine looks for fonts.

kind.description: Source kind: folder, file, memory, system or other.

location.description: Filesystem location; omitted for in-memory sources.

productFonts.description: The font environment of one product engine.

product.description: The product whose font engine this is.

defaultFont.description: The font substituted for any unavailable font when rendering; omitted when the engine exposes no configured default (it then uses an internal fallback).

sources.description: The font sources the engine scans, in configured order. Empty means the engine uses its platform defaults (typically the OS font folders).

v2/common/fonts-list-command.description: List each engine's font sources and its default fallback font.

options.name: --product
options.description: Product whose font engine to list; every product's when omitted.

v2/common/format-list.description: A product's formats document of aspose-cli schema: the formats the product declares.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

formats.description: The product's formats, in ordinal order of their ids.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

formatInfo.description: One format a product opens, converts to or renders to.

aliases.description: Other names the format id accepts.

uses.description: What the product does with the format: input, every command that opens a document reads it; convert-input, only convert reads it; convert, convert writes it; render, render writes it.

v2/common/input.description: Describes a file a command read.

encrypted.description: true when the file is encrypted and opens only with its password.

v2/common/license.description: License mode attached to a result whose engine ran without a license; a licensed result omits it.

v2/common/license-install-command.description: Validate a license file and install it for every compatible product.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Check the input, the output and the options, then stop without running the command or writing any file. A dry run that succeeds does not guarantee that the command succeeds.

options.name: --product
options.description: Install only for this product instead of detecting compatible products.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: Path to an Aspose license file (.lic) to install as this user's default.

v2/common/license-remove-command.description: Remove saved user licenses; env and project sources are left untouched.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Check the input, the output and the options, then stop without running the command or writing any file. A dry run that succeeds does not guarantee that the command succeeds.

options.name: --product
options.description: Remove only this product's saved user license.

v2/common/license-status.description: Result of aspose-cli license status: the effective, independently verified license status of every selected product; there is no first-product summary.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

products.description: The license status of each selected product.

sharedUserLicenseInstalled.description: Whether the shared user license, which every product reads, is installed.

identity.description: Opaque identity of this validated snapshot; absent when any selected source is invalid.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

productLicenseStatus.description: Effective license configuration and validation for one product.

mode.description: The license mode the product runs under.

source.description: Where the license comes from, such as an environment variable or the user license; omitted when there is none.

path.description: The license file's path, when the license is a file.

problem.description: Why the configured license was rejected; omitted when it is valid.

userLicenseInstalled.description: Whether a user license for this product is installed.

v2/common/license-status-command.description: Show whether licensing applies and which license source and mode are in effect.

options.name: --product
options.description: Inspect only this product.

v2/common/not-found-details.description: Details of an error whose code names a target that does not exist: a part the document does not contain, or a file. They state what was requested and what exists, so the caller can correct the request without another inspection. Operation errors add the operation's id and op.

subject.description: What was looked up, e.g. sheet, slide, bookmark or page.

requested.description: The name, number, range or path as the caller wrote it.

availableCount.description: How many targets of this kind the document contains; present for a target in a document.

path.description: The absolute path of the missing file; present for a file.

source.description: Where the missing file was configured, such as an environment variable; present when a setting names it.

sheet.description: The worksheet whose targets available lists; present for a target looked up on one sheet.

available.description: The names that exist, in document order; present for named targets and truncated to 50 when availableCount is larger.

id.description: The id of the failing operation, as its applied[] entry states it; present only for an operation error.

op.description: The failing operation's op name; present only for an operation error that states one.

index.description: The position of the failing operation in an object table batch, from 0; present only for such an operation.

at.description: The object table address that was looked up; present only for an object table address.

v2/common/operation-outcome.description: The stable wire result for one bounded edit operation.

id.description: Stable correlation id from the input batch.

itemsAffected.description: Number of product-owned items changed by the operation.

targets.description: Product-owned stable addresses of the changed items.

v2/common/output.description: Describes a file a command produced.

path.description: Absolute path of the produced file.

format.description: Format id of the produced file, e.g. pdf; for a companion file the engine writes beside it, such as a script of an HTML5 deck, the companion's file extension.

encrypted.description: true when the produced file is encrypted and opens only with its password; omitted when its format cannot carry a password.

v2/common/page-size.description: The size of a page in points (72 per inch) as a read reports it: both dimensions, and the preset they match in either orientation. An operation that sets a page size takes a preset or both dimensions under the same names.

preset.description: The preset the dimensions match; omitted when they match none.

v2/common/resource-budget.description: One discoverable default and hard maximum for a resource.

kind.description: What the budget limits, such as input-bytes.

default.description: The limit applied when nothing overrides it.

maximum.description: The hard safety maximum no override may exceed.

unit.description: The unit of default and maximum, such as bytes.

option.description: The command-line option that overrides the budget, when there is one.

environmentVariable.description: The environment variable that overrides the budget, when there is one.

enforcementStage.description: When the budget is enforced, such as before or while the input is read.

v2/common/result-window.description: How much of a larger collection a bounded read or search returned, and the option values that continue it. Every windowed result carries it as window, written after the payload and before license and warnings, so an agent always finds it in the same place.

unit.description: The unit returned and total count, e.g. page, block or hit.

returned.description: How many units this result returned.

total.description: How many units the selection holds; omitted when the read stopped before counting them all.

truncated.description: Whether units remain after the returned ones, or the last one was cut short.

next.description: The values of the command's options that return the next window, by option name without its leading dashes: the same command with these values returns it. Omitted when nothing remains.

notListedUnlessNamed.description: The kinds a read lists only when its --kind option names them, such as a spreadsheet's cells, that this read could have reached and did not list because no --kind named them; the same read with --kind and one of them lists those objects. Omitted when there are none.

v2/common/schema-catalog.description: Result of aspose-cli schema without an id: the products and their commands and formats, the platform commands, and the id of every document aspose-cli schema <id> prints.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

cliVersion.description: CLI version without build metadata, e.g. 2.0.0.

products.description: The products of this build, in the order the command line lists them.

commands.description: The platform commands, such as license and license install: each one's words after the executable name, in ordinal order. A command that only groups others has no document.

ids.description: The document ids aspose-cli schema <id> prints, in ordinal order: a command's options (<command>-command), a result's JSON Schema (<command>-result), an object table (ops) and its directory (ops/directory), a product's formats, and the diagnostics and budgets. Each name the directory lists is a part of the table, ops/<name>.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

catalogCommand.description: One command and what it does.

name.description: The command's words, such as convert or license install.

catalogProduct.description: One product: its engine, its commands and the formats it reads and writes.

id.description: Product id, the command-line word, e.g. cells.

engine.description: The engine's SDK package, e.g. Aspose.Cells.

commands.description: The product's commands, each one's words after the product id, in ordinal order.

loadFormats.description: Format ids every command of the product that opens a document reads; the formats document names those only convert reads.

v2/common/schema-command.description: Print the catalog of products, commands and document ids, or the document an id names.

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: Id of the document to print: one the catalog lists, or a part of an object table's schema that its directory names; omit it for the catalog.

v2/common/skill-install.description: Result of aspose-cli skill install: the agent skill bundled inside the binary was extracted to a target directory, ready for an agent framework to load.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

skill.description: The installed skill's name, e.g. aspose-cli-cells.

target.description: Absolute directory the skill was written to.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

v2/common/skill-install-command.description: Install a bundled Agent Skill for Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode.

options.name: --dir
options.description: Project root used without --user. Default: current working directory.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Check the input, the output and the options, then stop without running the command or writing any file. A dry run that succeeds does not guarantee that the command succeeds.

options.name: --host
options.description: Agent host whose standard skills directory should be used.

options.name: --target
options.description: Advanced: explicit parent directory; the selected Skill folder is created there.

options.name: --user
options.description: Install for the current user instead of the project.

arguments.name: skill
arguments.description: Bundled skill to install: aspose-cli-platform, aspose-cli-cells, aspose-cli-pdf, aspose-cli-slides, aspose-cli-words.

v2/common/skill-list.description: Result of aspose-cli skill list: skills bundled in this build.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

skills.description: Bundled skill packages available for installation.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

skillPackageInfo.description: One bundled Agent Skill and the supported host integrations.

hosts.description: Agent hosts with a known skills-directory convention.

v2/common/skill-list-command.description: List bundled Agent Skills and supported hosts.

v2/common/source-input.description: Describes a file a command read as the value of one of its options, such as the template or the content a file is created from: the facts of an InputInfo and the option.

format.description: Format id the file was read as, e.g. md.

encrypted.description: true when the file is encrypted and opens only with its password.

option.description: The option that named the file, e.g. --template.

v2/common/table-hit.description: One match of a search in a text row of the object table.

at.description: The address of the object whose row holds the match.

row.description: The text row that holds the match, such as text.

offset.description: Where the match starts in the row's text, counted in UTF-16 code units from 0; omitted for a match the engine's own search found, which gives no offset.

length.description: The match's length in UTF-16 code units; omitted with offset.

text.description: The matched text, as the row holds it, or as the engine's own search gives it.

rect.description: The rectangle the engine's own search gives for the match, as the engine writes it, such as a PDF text fragment's Rectangle, LLX,LLY,URX,URY in points; omitted for any other match.

v2/common/table-inventory.description: How many objects of each kind of content a document holds, counted with the engine's own collections: read for the kinds the object table addresses, which read lists, and notRead for the kinds it does not.

read.description: The counts of the kinds read lists, by inventory key.

notRead.description: The counts of the kinds read does not list, by inventory key.

v2/common/table-object.description: One object of a document, as the object table reads it.

at.description: The object's address, such as slide/256/shape/3; edit and read --at take it as it is.

kind.description: The object's kind, one of the kinds the product's ops schema lists.

props.description: Every row of the table the object has, by row name, as the engine gives it.

v2/common/table-op-report.description: What one operation of an edit left, read from the saved file after it was opened again: the object at the operation's address, or the value an action's engine call returned.

at.description: The address the operation named or created, in its canonical form; omitted for an action that returns no object. A position in it (a paragraph's, a run's, a cell's, a series', a point's) is the position the object had when the operation ran; a later operation of the batch can move what is at that position.

do.description: The action the operation ran; omitted for set, add, delete and move.

exists.description: Whether an object is at the address in the saved file; omitted where there is no address. An address by id is false after a delete that removed it. An address by position names the position: after a delete, true with the rows of the object that moved into it, false only when nothing is there; neither says whether the delete removed what it named.

now.description: Every row of the object that is at the address in the saved file, after the whole batch; omitted when no object is there. At a position, this is what the saved file holds there, which a later operation of the batch may have put there.

returned.description: The value the action's engine call returned; omitted for set, add, delete and move and for a call that returns nothing.

v2/common/unchecked-operation.description: An operation of the batch that an edit's verification did not read back.

id.description: The operation's id in the batch.

reason.description: Why the verification did not read the operation back.

v2/common/verification-issue.description: A problem found while verifying an edited output that had already been produced. Any issue makes the verification ok:false and the command exit 8.

code.description: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE identifier an agent can branch on.

location.description: The affected item's address in the targets syntax <unit>/<address>, such as page/3, slide/2/shape/4 or cell/Sheet1!A1, with names escaped as targets escape them; omitted unless the issue concerns exactly one item.

v2/common/version.description: Result of aspose-cli --version --output-format json: the build identity.

schema.description: URI of the JSON schema this result conforms to.

cliVersion.description: CLI version without build metadata, e.g. 1.0.0; the same value as the schema catalog's cliVersion.

artifactVersion.description: Full artifact version, as plain --version prints it, when it carries build metadata beyond cliVersion; omitted when the two are equal.

sourceRevision.description: Root source revision embedded by the distribution build.

buildDirty.description: Whether tracked source changes were present during the build.

enginePins.description: The engine package and version compiled for each product.

warnings.description: Warnings the agent is expected to act on (for example EVALUATION_MODE: tell the user about the evaluation watermark). Omitted when empty.

enginePin.description: The engine package one product is compiled with.

engine.description: Engine package compiled for the product, e.g. Aspose.Cells.

v2/common/warning.description: A non-fatal condition of a command that succeeded. Warnings are part of the public contract.

location.description: The affected item's address in the targets syntax <unit>/<address>, such as page/3, slide/2/shape/4 or cell/Sheet1!A1, with names escaped as targets escape them; omitted when the condition concerns no single item, such as the whole document.

details.description: Structured context, with the keys an error's details use, such as the id and op of the operation a warning is about.

affectsCompleteness.description: Whether this condition leaves the output or its visual evidence incomplete, or different from the input; an edit's verification reports it as an issue when it is about content the edit lost.
